title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: What makes this role's source material different from every other role's in this curriculum?
options: It is more sensitive and more heavily regulated
There is no ground truth — the material is incompatible accounts, and the incompatibility is the evidence rather than noise around a signal
It is unstructured rather than tabular
It arrives continuously rather than in batches
questions.explanation: Which means "accurate to the source" stops being a sufficient standard: a summary can be faithful to all three statements and still be worse than useless.

questions.prompt: Why is harmonization not a hallucination?
options: Because the model is following its instructions correctly
Because coherence is what summarization *is* — the operation compresses by finding a through-line, so nothing is fabricated and every sentence checks out against a source
Because the errors are small enough to fall within tolerance
Because the model discloses its uncertainty
questions.explanation: Which is why 101 M6's answer — verify the claim against the source — does not work here. The error is in the relationship between the summary and the *state of the evidence*.

questions.prompt: Which harmonization mechanism describes a summary landing on the middle version of a contested detail?
options: Smoothing
Averaging
Confidence flattening
Narrative completion
questions.explanation: And it is a form of weighing performed invisibly, with no record that a choice was made. Smoothing merges accounts into a characterization nobody gave; flattening loses the hedge; completion supplies the joins a narrative needs.

questions.prompt: Where exactly is the line this module draws?
options: AI may not be used on investigation material at all
AI may summarize but a human must approve the summary
A model may locate conflicts; only a human may resolve them
AI may assess consistency but not assign credibility
questions.explanation: Locating is factual and checkable in seconds. Resolving is a credibility determination. D is the specific error the module warns about — consistency assessment *is* resolution.

questions.prompt: Which request crosses the line while appearing analytical?
options: "List every point on which these accounts differ."
"Which of these accounts is most consistent with the other evidence?"
"Quote the exact words each account uses about the meeting."
"Which matters at issue does this account not address?"
questions.explanation: It takes conflicts you legitimately located and asks for a ranking against a standard, which is a finding. A, C and D are all rung-two requests about what the material says.

questions.prompt: Why does the module say a standard of proof makes this a bright line?
options: Because standards of proof are set by statute and cannot be delegated
Because the balance of probabilities is not a threshold to check a number against — it is an instruction to weigh, so a model that weighs has applied your standard and you cannot say how
Because different jurisdictions apply different standards
Because standards of proof require documented reasoning for audit purposes
questions.explanation: Which leaves you with a conclusion, an impression of why, and no reconstructable path from evidence to finding — the one thing the report has to contain and the first thing the other side attacks.

questions.prompt: What does the module say about an account that omits a matter at issue?
options: It should be treated as agreement with the other accounts
It is not a denial — the statement looks identical whether the person wasn't there, doesn't remember, wasn't asked, or is avoiding it
It should be excluded until clarified
Omissions are only significant if the witness was directly asked
questions.explanation: Four completely different evidential states, one identical statement — and models fill gaps unmarked, which makes the omission the thing a fluent summary most reliably disappears.

questions.prompt: What three questions does the module substitute for "what does this account establish?"
options: Who, what, and when
Contains, omits, and contradicts — kept as three separate answers that are never merged
Reliable, unreliable, and unknown
Corroborated, uncorroborated, and disputed
questions.explanation: Merging them is harmonization performed by you rather than by the model, and the document is no better for having been assembled by hand. Question two also requires a list of matters at issue, which is why intake structure pays off here.
